newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egypt says its Israel-PLO peace effort failing.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says its Israel-PLO peace effort failing.

text.p: Egypt's foreign minister said in an interview published on Friday that Egyptian efforts to break a deadlock between Israel and the Palestinians were leading nowhere.
Interviewed by the Hebrew daily Haaretz, Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Israel was to blame for the failure.
Underscoring the crisis in peacemaking, Israeli soldiers shot and wounded three Palestinians during clashes that erupted in the West Bank city of Hebron.
The city has been the scene of almost daily unrest since a right-wing Jewish woman put up posters two weeks ago depicting the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
"I'll say it simply: After six weeks of attempts and contacts, until now the Egyptian initiative has not achieved anything," Moussa said.
"There has been no progress and the Israeli government has not budged from its position...The responsibility for the tension rests with Israel," he said.
Moussa accused Israel of refusing to stand by signed accords, citing Israel's expansion of Jewish settlements among other issues.
He urged Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to reconsider his policies. Netanyahu insists Israel's peace deals with the PLO allow for settlement expansion.

By agreement of Israel, the PLO and the United States, the main peacemaking sponsor, Egypt has been trying to restart the talks frozen for four months since Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Palestinians said on Thursday mutual confidence-building measures including opening of an airport and construction of a sea port in Gaza could help revive the talks. Both were agreed upon under interim peace deals.
Moussa said Egypt would be willing also to mediate in any Israeli peacemaking with Syria and Lebanon.

"We are always willing to help if they ask it of us...But what is there to do? The mutual trust has collapsed in the whole peace process. There is no more goodwill and the atmosphere is gloomy," he said.

Negotiations between Israel and Syria broke off last year. Syria has demanded an Israeli commitment to withdraw from the strategic Golan Heights it captured in the 1967 Middle East war before renewing talks.

Moussa said in light of the peacemaking crisis, Egypt had yet to decide whether to attend a regional economic summit in Qatar in November. Several Arab states have said they will not attend due to Israel's planned participation.

"The atmosphere surrounding the Qatar conference is gloomy. The reason is that all regional trust has been lost. Egypt's position regarding Qatar has not been finalised. We are following the developments and according to them we will decide," he said.
